title: Inner-anodyne locality of homotopy Segal spaces
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, the simplex category $\Delta$, spaces and coherent mapping spaces from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Fix a universe of small objects and enlarge the ambient universe to form $\mathcal P_\Delta=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$, where $\mathcal S$ is the infinity category of small spaces. For a small simplicial set $K$, write $dK\in\mathcal P_\Delta$ for the diagram whose value in degree $n$ is the discrete space $K_n$. An inner-anodyne map of simplicial sets is a map in the smallest class containing all inclusions $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ for $n\geq2$, $0<i<n$, and closed under pushouts, small transfinite compositions and retracts, with colimits here taken degreewise in sets. Let $W\in\mathcal P_\Delta$ satisfy the homotopy Segal condition: for every $n\geq2$, the consecutive-edge restriction
$$W_n\longrightarrow W_1\times_{W_0}\cdots\times_{W_0}W_1$$
is an equivalence, with all products over $W_0$ interpreted as homotopy pullbacks. For every inner-anodyne $u:K\to L$, restriction is an equivalence of coherent mapping spaces
$$u^*:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P_\Delta}(dL,W)\xrightarrow{\simeq}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P_\Delta}(dK,W).$$
The comparison is natural in $u$ and $W$. No completeness condition is imposed on $W$.

source.place: Definitions 6.1–6.3 and Corollary 6.6 with its proof, specialized to the terminal monoidal category; compare Gepner–Haugseng 1312.3178v4, proof of Theorem 5.2.5, and Rezk math/9811037, Remark 10.2. Read online; archival copy WANTED in report.md. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical fact.

proof.text: Fix $W$ as in the statement and let $\mathcal E_W$ be the class of arrows $a:A\to B$ in $\mathcal P_\Delta$ for which $\operatorname{Map}(B,W)\to\operatorname{Map}(A,W)$ is an equivalence. The presheaf category has all small colimits by [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-free-cocompletion], applied to the small category $\Delta$. By [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], mapping out of any such colimit into $W$ is the corresponding limit of mapping spaces. Thus $\mathcal E_W$ contains identities and is closed under composition, two-out-of-three and retracts: these assertions follow by applying the mapping-space functor and the corresponding rules for equivalences of spaces. It is closed under cobase change, since mapping out of a pushout gives a homotopy pullback and a pullback of an equivalence is an equivalence.

source.place: Definitions 6.1–6.3 and proof of Corollary 6.6, terminal monoidal specialization; degreewise cell transfer made explicit.

proof.text: The same class is closed under small transfinite compositions. For a continuous sequence $(A_\alpha)_{\alpha\leq\lambda}$ whose successor maps belong to $\mathcal E_W$, prove by transfinite induction that $A_0\to A_\beta$ belongs to $\mathcal E_W$. The zero case is the identity and the successor case is composition. At a nonzero limit $\beta$, [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] gives $\operatorname{Map}(A_\beta,W)\simeq\lim_{\alpha<\beta}\operatorname{Map}(A_\alpha,W)$. The restrictions to $A_0$ give an objectwise equivalence from this diagram to the constant diagram with value $\operatorname{Map}(A_0,W)$ by the inductive hypothesis. Its limit is that value: the nonempty ordinal $\beta$ has contractible nerve, contracted to its initial element $0$. Taking limits gives precisely restriction to $A_0$. Hence $\mathcal E_W$ is weakly saturated.

source.place: Definitions 6.1–6.3 and proof of Corollary 6.6, terminal monoidal specialization; degreewise cell transfer made explicit.

proof.text: Take the terminal monoidal infinity category $C=*$. In [def-coef-segal-presheaf-localization] its structural category $C_\otimes$ is $\Delta$: there is one label list in each degree and cartesian transport is unique. The represented labelled simplex is $d\Delta^n$, and the pullback formula of [lem-coef-labelled-spine-prism-horn-calculus] identifies the represented labelled horn with $d\Lambda_i^n$. Write $S_n$ for the labelled spine, the iterated presheaf pushout of $n$ edge representables over vertex representables. By the evaluation equivalence of [lem-coef-space-yoneda-density] and the conversion of pushouts to homotopy pullbacks in [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], restriction along $S_n\to d\Delta^n$ identifies with the given map $W_n\to W_1\times_{W_0}\cdots\times_{W_0}W_1$. Therefore every spine inclusion belongs to $\mathcal E_W$. This uses the homotopy Segal hypothesis alone.

source.place: Definitions 6.1–6.3 and proof of Corollary 6.6, terminal monoidal specialization; degreewise cell transfer made explicit.

proof.text: Prove by induction on $n\geq2$ that every $d\Lambda_i^n\to d\Delta^n$, $0<i<n$, belongs to $\mathcal E_W$. For $n=2$ the only horn is the two-edge spine $S_2$, so Step 3 applies. Assume the assertion in dimensions less than $n$. The finite filtration clause of [lem-coef-labelled-spine-prism-horn-calculus], with $C=*$ as in Step 3, expresses $S_n\to d\Lambda_i^n$ as a finite composite of pushouts of inner horn inclusions of dimensions strictly less than $n$. Each attaching map belongs to $\mathcal E_W$ by the induction hypothesis, so Steps 1–2 imply $S_n\to d\Lambda_i^n\in\mathcal E_W$. The composite $S_n\to d\Lambda_i^n\to d\Delta^n$ is the spine inclusion of Step 3. Two-out-of-three now gives $d\Lambda_i^n\to d\Delta^n\in\mathcal E_W$, completing the induction.

source.place: Definitions 6.1–6.3 and proof of Corollary 6.6, terminal monoidal specialization; degreewise cell transfer made explicit.

proof.text: We must compare the statement's degreewise-set weak saturation with the presheaf weak saturation; no preservation of arbitrary pushouts by $d$ is assumed. An ordinary inner horn inclusion has the left lifting property against every inner fibration by definition. This lifting property is closed under pushouts (transpose a square using the pushout property), transfinite composites (choose compatible diagonal lifts successively and glue at limits), and retracts (compose the square and diagonal with the retract maps). Consequently the given $u$ has this lifting property. By [lem-coef-inner-horn-cell-generation], $u$ is a retract of a small continuous transfinite composite of pushouts of small coproducts of ordinary inner horns, with colimits degreewise in sets. These are exactly the hypotheses of [lem-coef-discrete-inner-cell-transfer]; hence $du$ belongs to the presheaf weakly saturated class generated by the discrete inner horn maps.

source.place: Definitions 6.1–6.3 and proof of Corollary 6.6, terminal monoidal specialization; degreewise cell transfer made explicit.

proof.text: Step 4 puts every generator of that presheaf weakly saturated class in $\mathcal E_W$, and Steps 1–2 show its closure under all three generating operations. Step 5 therefore gives $du\in\mathcal E_W$, which is the required restriction equivalence. These are the actual restriction maps, not selected inverses. For a commutative square of maps of simplicial sets, the two iterated restrictions agree; for $W\to W'$, postcomposition commutes with restriction. The composition laws and their higher coherences in the presheaf category give naturality in both $u$ and $W$. No completeness or Reedy fibrancy assumption has entered.
